read-build-and-write-a-conversation.label: Read, Build, and Write a Conversation
read-build-and-write-a-conversation.summary: Use numbers, time, schedules, and complete questions to arrange a simple everyday plan.

read-build-and-write-a-conversation-choi.prompt: Which question asks what time someone works?
read-build-and-write-a-conversation-choi.hint: Choose the clock-time question from Module 7.

help.concept: A schedule conversation needs a question that asks for clock time.
help.hint_1: Reuse a complete pattern you practiced earlier in this course.
help.hint_2: Read or listen to the whole exchange before answering.

make-plan.title: Ask what time
make-plan.bodyMarkdown:
**A:** Akilè ou travay?

**B:** Setè edmi.

**A:** Èske ou etidye kreyòl chak jou?

**B:** Wi, mwen etidye kreyòl chak jou.

This combines the question patterns from Module 6 with the time language from Module 7.

count-things.title: Konbyen…?
count-things.bodyMarkdown:
Numbers can enter the conversation naturally:

**A:** Konbyen liv ou genyen?

**B:** Mwen gen twa liv.

You only need the 1–20 number system from Module 7 for this beginner exchange.

schedule-chunks.title: jòdi a, kounyeya, chak jou
schedule-chunks.bodyMarkdown:
Small time expressions make your meaning clearer:

- **jòdi a** — today
- **kounyeya** — now
- **chak jou** — every day

Use them with sentences you already know instead of adding new tense grammar.
